name: Sabayon Linux
description: Italian Gentoo-based distro that precompiled the world so you didn't have to. Slipped into the abyss at 14 after the maintainer waved the Entropy package manager a fond farewell.

name: Scientific Linux
description: Fermilab and CERN's beloved RHEL rebuild, kept particle physicists out of dependency hell for fifteen years. Rested in peace once CentOS 8 showed up to take over the beaker.

name: MagpieOS
description: Bangladeshi Arch spin named after the national bird, crafted to spare mortals from the command-line rites of vanilla Arch. Flew into the sunset at barely two when the solo student maintainer archived the repo.

name: Antergos
description: Arch for people who didn't want to type 'pacman -S' fifty times. Pulled the Numix-themed plug at six, citing a single maintainer who'd had enough of being on call.

name: MEPIS Linux
description: Debian-derived, KDE-flavoured and famously easy on the grandparents. Died of natural causes at 10 when its founder wandered off toward Lubuntu pastures.

name: Ankur Bangla
description: Pioneering Bangladeshi distro that brought Bangla GNOME, Mukti fonts, and out-of-the-box Bengali typing to the masses. Bowed out after its 2012 Shishir release once upstream distros finally learned to render Indic script.

name: Corel Linux
description: Corel's very public attempt to make Linux the next Windows. Survived a single birthday cake before the bean counters rolled the credits. It was about 1 year old.

name: Ubuntu Software Center
description: Replaced Synaptic with something that wouldn't scare the people who asked why their printer wouldn't print. Stepped aside at 5 in favour of the GNOME Software store.

name: Bazaar
description: Canonical's distributed version control system that tried to be nicer than git by, well, not being git. Emigrated to the attic at 13 with the rest of Launchpad's quieter tools.

name: Arista Transcoder
description: Sweet little GNOME transcoder that wrapped FFmpeg in a friendly face. Pushed up daisies at 2 when its developer got a real job and the GStreamer pipe under it rusted through.

name: Firefox Send
description: Mozilla's sleek, end-to-end encrypted file sharing tool that let you send self-destructing links. Shuttered at 3 after malware operators realized it was also the world's most convenient drop box.

name: Ubuntu One
description: Canonical's cloud-storage, music-streaming, file-syncing 'we can compete with Dropbox' bet. Dropped the bass for the last time at 5; 90 days later, all your files were someone else's problem.

name: Mozilla Persona
description: Mozilla's password-free, email-as-identity login system that nobody but nerds ever adopted. Joined the choir invisible at 3, replaced by 'just use OAuth, you cowards'.

name: Google Reader
description: Not Linux, but the FOSS-adjacent RSS reader that half the open-source web relied on. Murdered at 7 to make a quarterly number look better; the resulting petitions became their own genre.

name: Flock (browser)
description: Chromium-based social-networking browser loved by the early Web 2.0 crowd. Closed its tabs for the last time at 6 when its users had all moved to actual Facebook.
